item.title: Auburn Avenue’s Coffee Was Black reclaims coffee’s African roots
item.description: Coffee Was Black is a coffee shop on Auburn Avenue that celebrates Black heritage and entrepreneurship, offering a unique blend of coffee and culture while honoring the legacy of Mrs. Geneva Morton Haugabrooks, a successful Black female business owner from the Jim Crow era. item.title: The Silent Killer of Black Maternal Health
item.description: Obria Smith, a 31-year-old Atlanta native, tragically passed away from complications of eclampsia, a condition that disproportionately affects African American women and is running rampant in the US, with cases of pre-eclampsia rising 25% between 1987 and 2004.
